name: 瓦尔德拉克
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:260
who: Valdrak of the Emberhorn clan, a fire-horn demon-kin, head of the Redemption Army and master of the forge of the Horn City, a hundred and sixty-two in 742 and looking just over thirty ever since he became a legend that year: about 208 cm, very tall, broad-backed and heavy-boned, standing like a crag of burnt black rock. Deep grey skin, as if tempered in volcanic ash. The left horn glossy black; the right horn broken off just above the ring of obsidian at its root, twenty notches cut into the stump, always glowing red as if burning inside. Black-brown hair with dark ember-red undertones, cropped very short so the horns show. Red eyes that glance down at your feet before your face. Forge burns on both arms, old scars on the chest and left shoulder. A terse, hard, unhurried air.
build: 208 cm, very tall and heavy-boned: a broad back and shoulders, thick arms, a heavy, even stride.
palette: volcanic ash grey and burnt black, forge red and orange, dull black iron, worn boot brown
casual: His everyday wear in the Horn City: a heavy suit of dark armour he forged himself at the forge, thick plates of black iron with a dull red glow along the seams, over a dark padded coat, buckled all the way up to the collar; a plain dark cloak hooked on one shoulder; on his feet a pair of old boots patched again and again since the caravan years. In his right hand a long-handled heavy blade, also forged by his own hands, held low at an angle. He looks down at your feet first, a terse, steady look.
private: At the forge when the day's work is done: a sleeveless dark linen work shirt, a heavy scorched leather forge apron, dark trousers and the old patched boots, the forge burns showing on his bare arms. He holds a bent iron spear shaft in his bare hands, straightening it just by gripping it, the iron glowing red where his fingers close. A quiet, absorbed look.
battle: At the head of the Redemption Army on the seven bends of the lava road: the self-forged dark armour buckled tight to the throat, heavy pauldrons and gauntlets, a dark cloak, the old patched boots. He grips the long-handled heavy blade in both hands, angled low across his body, the twenty notches on the broken horn glowing red; braced at the very front, a hard, level look.
formal: At the stone by the city gate on the day the names are read: a long dark iron-grey wool coat of the Horn City buttoned to the throat, a dark red sash, a short black cloak over the left shoulder, the old boots polished, the broken horn left bare. He stands very upright with his hands at his sides, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait from slightly below with the camera tilted, the face large, the red eyes glancing down past the viewer as if at their feet, a hard, quiet look; the broken right horn with its twenty glowing red notches sharp in the frame. Hard orange light from a forge below on one side. Foreground blur: drifting ash, sparks off an anvil and a red-hot spear shaft held in his fist. He wears the self-forged dark armour buckled to the collar.

name: 伊德娜
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:314
who: Idna of the Anvil family, a bull-horned demon-kin woman of the Thunder-Gaol folk and second-in-command of the Redemption Army, who spent forty-nine years in the seventh pit: ninety-one in 742, with the body of a woman just past forty. About 196 cm, a head taller than most men, broad-shouldered and heavy-boned. Deep bronze-coloured skin. Her horns were sawn off flat in the pit: two flat stumps on top of her head, hidden under two braids plaited from the hair at her temples. Short copper-red hair. A broad face with small, bright orange eyes. An old brand scar on the left collarbone. Pale scars on both shins with a glint of white bone beneath, and a slight drag in her left foot. A flat, few-worded, steady air: she always marks the way back first.
face: FACE, as in the references: a broad, strong-boned woman's face of about forty, NOT young: small, bright orange almond eyes under level copper-red brows, fine lines at their corners; a straight nose; a firm, closed mouth. Deep bronze-coloured skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft warm brown.
build: 196 cm, very tall and heavy-boned: broad shoulders, a thick back, arms thicker than most men's, a very full bust, a solid waist and full hips.
palette: copper red and deep bronze, ember orange, worn leather brown, a little pit-iron grey
casual: Her Redemption Army gear: old leather armour with a plate of iron nailed onto each shoulder, melted down from the shackle rings she brought up out of the seventh pit, over a dark wool tunic, dark trousers and heavy boots; a cloth sash round her waist tied with seven knots, one for each bend of the road. In her hand a long spear whose butt is capped with iron, worn bright from scoring lines on the ground; she holds it at an angle, the butt resting on the ground. A flat, steady look.
private: Off duty in the Horn City: a loose undyed wool tunic with long sleeves belted with the seven-knotted sash, wide trousers and her boots, which she never takes off even to sleep; the braids over her horn stumps a little lopsided, plaited by a child. She eats standing up, as she did in the pit, a heel of bread in one hand and a cup in the other, a quiet, easy look.
battle: Holding the way back: the old leather armour with the iron shoulder plates buckled tight, leather bracers and greaves over her scarred shins, the seven-knotted sash. She grips the long spear in both hands, slanted low across her body like a bar across a road, braced and immovable over a line she has just scored in the black ground, a level, unblinking look.
formal: On the day the names are read at the city gate, the only dressing up she does: the old leather armour cleaned and oiled, the iron shoulder plates polished, a clean dark grey wool cloak pinned at the throat, the seven-knotted sash retied, the braids freshly plaited over her horn stumps. She stands very upright with the spear held at an angle at her side, a grave, quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the small orange eyes looking at the viewer level and unafraid, one big hand on the spear shaft. Hot red-orange light rising from lava below on one side. Foreground blur: drifting ash, the iron butt of a spear scoring a line in black ground and the knotted end of a cloth sash. She wears the old leather armour with the iron plates on the shoulders.

name: 莉西娅
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:558
who: Lithia Bloodthorn, once of the Night-Crimson house, a succubus demon-kin of the feast-born bloodline and mistress of the Red Garden, who took the head seat at the seven-night ball in 758 and has not aged a day since: a hundred and twenty-eight then, looking just over thirty. About 172 cm, tall and graceful, the neck and shoulders straight. Long silver-white hair hanging loose below the waist, no longer braided, a few short lengths of blood-thorn vine caught in it, their thorns dark red; once a year in late autumn they put out tiny red flowers. Short pointed ears. Deep crimson eyes, a little narrowed, as if looking at you through a wine glass. Thin black gloves she never takes off in company. A courteous, sharp-tongued, composed air; when she is afraid she smiles more.
build: 172 cm, tall and graceful: a straight neck and shoulders, a full bust, a very narrow waist and full hips.
palette: silver-white and deep crimson, black leather and black silk, a little thorn red
casual: Her dress for sitting at a table: a long deep crimson wool dress with a high collar and close sleeves, a black cloak over it buttoned to the throat, thin black leather gloves with a band of black silk at each wrist; at her waist the small leather wallet in which she notes who sat where and who spoke first; pinned inside the collar a slim silver needle, the house badge of the twelfth seat. One gloved hand rests at her collar, a courteous, attentive smile.
private: Alone in the smallest greenhouse of the Red Garden after a banquet: a soft ivory blouse with a high neck and long sleeves, a long dark wine-red skirt, a plain dark apron, soft shoes, the silver hair loose with its thorns. Her gloves are off and tucked into the apron string; on the knuckle of her right forefinger a few small inked dots. She holds a pair of pruning shears and a cut stem of small white roses, a quiet, unguarded smile.
battle: On the road to a table that may turn into a trap: a deep crimson riding habit with a fitted jacket and a long split skirt, the black cloak buttoned to the throat, black gloves banded with black silk, tall black riding boots, the leather wallet at her waist. She carries no blade, for within a banquet truce she never draws one.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: poised and alert, the weight on one foot, a calm smile that does not reach the eyes, one gloved hand raised a little with the palm open as if to say you may refuse, the other holding the small leather wallet; she carries no weapon.
formal: Hostess of the Red Garden's great banquet: a long deep crimson silk gown with a high collar of black lace closed at the throat, long close sleeves and a long train, a short black cape lined in dark red, black gloves banded with black silk at the wrists, the blood-thorn in her loose silver hair in bloom with tiny red flowers, the twelfth seat's silver needle pinned at the collar. She stands very upright with the gloved hands folded at her waist, a calm, faintly dangerous smile.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the crimson eyes looking at the viewer with a tired, courteous half-smile after a night-long banquet, one black-gloved hand resting on an overturned silver cup. Cold pale dawn light from one side. Foreground blur: a row of overturned silver cups on a stone balustrade, blood-thorn twigs and drifting tiny red flowers. She wears the black cloak buttoned to the throat over the deep crimson dress.

name: 艾芙琳·血棘
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:612
who: Evelyn Bloodthorn, a blood-mage demon-kin of the feast-born bloodline and head of the twelfth seat of the twelve banquet houses, whose house badge is a needle, the youngest at the long table; twenty-three in 758 and looking just past twenty: not tall, about 163 cm, sitting and standing very straight with her hands kept still. Black hair pinned up low at the nape, a single lock of dark red hanging behind one ear. Rose-red eyes that look at people's hands first. On the pad of her left forefinger a neat row of tiny needle pricks. A quiet, earnest, timid air: at the seven-night ball she was too frightened to stand up, and turned her cup upside down on the table instead of drinking.
build: 163 cm, evenly built and very upright: a medium bust, a narrow waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: black and deep grey, rose red, a little dark red, rose-paper ivory, silver
casual: Her dress after the seven nights, all in black: a long black wool dress with a high collar buttoned to the throat and long close sleeves, a narrow black belt from which hangs a slim, long leather case holding needles, rose paper and a small vial of her own blood for writing invitations. She holds a folded invitation of pale rose paper in both hands, a shy, careful look.
private: Sleepless in the greenhouse in late autumn: a long-sleeved black linen dress with a soft charcoal knitted shawl over the shoulders, soft shoes, the low knot of black hair loosened a little. She holds a fallen sprig of blood-thorn with its tiny red flowers in her palm, a quiet, tired look.
battle: On a banquet night when someone at the table may draw: the black dress with a short black cloak buttoned to the throat, the slim leather case at her belt, soft black shoes. She carries no weapon; she holds a silver cup upside down in one hand and her slim silver needle in the other.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: frightened but standing her ground, the shoulders drawn up, the feet together, a pale, steady expression, holding a silver cup turned upside down in one hand and a slim silver needle in the other; she carries no weapon.
formal: The robe of the twelfth seat, as she wore it through the seven nights: a long deep grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat and a single needle embroidered in silver thread at each cuff, a narrow dark red sash, black shoes. She stands very upright with her hands pressed together in front of her, a timid but steady look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the rose-red eyes lifting from the viewer's hands to their face, a shy, steady look; her slim fingers turn a silver cup upside down on a dark tablecloth. Warm candlelight from one side. Foreground blur: the rim of an overturned cup, a fine silver needle and drifting slips of pale rose paper. She wears the high-collared black dress.

name: 贝内特·执壶
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:668
who: Bennet Ewerbearer, a blood-mage demon-kin of the feast-born bloodline and the old sommelier of the banquet city, who has poured the twelve houses' oath-wine and kept their oath ledger for a hundred and seventy-eight years; a hundred and ninety-eight in 758 and looking about fifty: about 186 cm, tall and thin, narrow-shouldered and long-handed, the back a little stooped from bending to pour. Grey-white hair combed back very neatly. A long face with thin lips. Eyes once deep red, now faded to the colour of rust; he looks at your cup before your face. On the inside of his right wrist a small ewer branded into the skin, its spout toward the palm. His pouring hand has never shaken. A flat, precise, dryly cutting air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a long, lean man's face of about fifty, NOT young: fine lines at the eye corners and beside the mouth, narrow rust-red eyes, straight grey brows, thin lips held level, clean-shaven. Pale clean skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 186 cm, tall and thin: narrow shoulders, long arms and hands, the back slightly stooped.
palette: black and white, faded rust red, polished silver, black ledger leather with brass
casual: His sommelier's dress: a long black coat buttoned up to the collar, white gloves, dark trousers and polished black shoes; under his left arm the oath ledger, bound in black leather with a brass clasp; in his right hand his family's old silver ewer with a long, thin spout. He stands with his hands in front of him, a flat, attentive look.
private: Counting cups alone in the empty hall after a banquet: the coat off, a plain white shirt buttoned to the collar with the sleeves turned back once, a black waistcoat, dark trousers, the gloves off so the brand of the little ewer shows on his right wrist. He holds a short stack of silver cups in one hand, counting them with the other, a quiet, dry look.
battle: Going down into the cellar with a lamp to count who is in the house: the long black coat buttoned to the collar, white gloves, the oath ledger under one arm. He holds up a lantern in his right hand; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the cellar outfit: alert and steady, the stooped back straightened, a firm, careful expression, holding up a lantern in one hand with the oath ledger under the other arm; he carries no weapon.
formal: As head sommelier on a great banquet night: a long black tailcoat with a high stiff collar and small silver buttons, a narrow wine-red sash, fresh white gloves. He stands very upright, the silver ewer held level in one hand and the oath ledger flat against his chest with the other, a grave, impassive look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the rust-red eyes lowered to the viewer's cup rather than their face, a flat, unreadable look; his white-gloved hand tilts the long thin spout of a silver ewer, a thin dark red stream pouring without a drop spilled. Warm low candlelight from one side. Foreground blur: the rim of a silver cup, the brass clasp of a black ledger and drifting candle smoke. He wears the long black coat buttoned to the collar.

name: 莎蒂
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:724
who: Sadie, a demon-kin girl of the long-lived folk, the smallest of the seven children once shut in the cellar under the Red Garden ballroom, who keeps the chair nearest the door and leads hidden people through the root tunnels; her folk grow like human children for their first years and then very slowly, so she is about thirty-eight but looks fifteen or sixteen: small and slight, about 156 cm, wholly covered by her clothes, moving without a sound. No horns. Pale lilac hair she cuts short herself with scissors, the ends uneven. Amber eyes that shine in the dark like two lamp-points. A pale face. Around her neck on a thin cord a small copper hoop-plate taken from a wine barrel. A quiet, watchful air; when she is afraid she counts to seven under her breath.
palette: dark wine red and charcoal, pale lilac, amber, a little copper
casual: Her clothes in the Red Garden: a dark wine-red short coat with narrow cuffs, buttoned to the collar, over a long dark grey dress to the shins, dark stockings and soft-soled shoes that make no sound; nothing on her that jingles, no bell and no loose buckle; the copper hoop-plate on its thin cord at her neck. She stands quietly with her hands together, a watchful look.
private: In a quiet corner of the root tunnels: a long-sleeved dark grey knitted dress with narrow cuffs, soft shoes, the short hair a little messy. She holds a small plate of salted biscuits in both hands, carried for someone who forgets to eat, a soft, quiet look.
battle: Leading hidden people through the dark root tunnels: the dark short coat buttoned up under a short dark hooded cape, the cuffs and hems tied close, soft shoes; nothing that makes a sound. She holds a small shuttered lantern low in one hand and raises the forefinger of the other to her lips; she carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the root-tunnel outfit: alert and light on her feet, the shoulders drawn in, one forefinger raised to her lips for silence, the other hand holding a small shuttered lantern low; she does not fight.
formal: When the Red Garden holds a banquet: a long dark wine-red dress with a high collar buttoned to the throat and narrow cuffs, a small black ribbon at the collar, the copper hoop-plate on its cord. She stands very upright with her hands folded in front, a quiet, solemn look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the amber eyes shining in the dark as she looks at the viewer, one forefinger raised to her lips. The faint glow of a single lamp far behind her on one side. Foreground blur: the rough wall of a root tunnel scratched with rows of short tally lines, and drifting dust. She wears the dark wine-red short coat buttoned to the collar.

name: 莫尔图斯
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:904
who: Mortus, a demon-kin of the white-bone folk and a child of a bell-tower keeper's family, who has written down the names of the westward caravan for eighty years and lights a tiny clay lamp for each of its dead; a hundred and fifty-seven in 742 and looking about thirty: about 184 cm, tall and thin with narrow shoulders. Skin pale almost to translucence; along the left side of the jaw a strip of bone shows, white as crystal. Short black hair falling a little over the brow. Ice-blue eyes with no sleep in them and no warmth. Long, ink-stained fingers. An old burn scar on the back of the left hand. A bell clapper carved from bone hangs at his neck on a cord. A quiet, exact air with a dry, unsmiling humour.
build: 184 cm, tall and thin: narrow shoulders, long fingers, a very straight back.
palette: charcoal and ash grey, bone white, ice blue, a little lamp amber
casual: His caravan clothes: a long charcoal-grey robe buttoned up to the throat, the cuffs bound close with strips of cloth so they will not smear the ink, dark trousers and plain boots; at his waist a small cloth pouch holding a handful of ash from the gate passage of Rain City; on his back a wooden lamp chest whose little compartments hold thousands of thumb-sized clay lamps; the bone bell clapper on its cord at his neck. He holds an open register and a pen, a calm, exact look.
private: Sitting up through the night by the register cart: a plain dark grey wool shirt buttoned to the neck with the cuffs tied, dark trousers, soft boots, the lamp chest set down. He holds a tiny lit clay lamp cupped in both hands as if shielding it from the wind, a quiet, gentle look.
battle: Walking a field after a battle to name the dead: the charcoal robe buttoned to the throat under a grey hooded travelling cloak, the cuffs bound, the lamp chest on his back. He holds a small lit clay lamp in one hand and the open register against his chest with the other; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the battlefield outfit: upright and still, a level, careful gaze, holding a small lit clay lamp in one hand and the open register against his chest with the other; he does not fight.
formal: Reading out the caravan's dead at a memorial: a clean long ash-grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat, the cuffs neatly bound, a dark grey mantle over the shoulders, the bone bell clapper on its cord outside the robe. He holds the register closed against his chest with both hands, standing very straight, a grave, polite look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer without blinking, a faint, dry look, one ink-stained hand cupping a tiny clay lamp near his face. Warm small lamplight from below on one side against a cold dusk. Foreground blur: rows of tiny lit clay lamps in the open compartments of a wooden chest, drifting grey ash and a bone bell clapper on its cord. He wears the charcoal-grey robe buttoned to the throat.

name: 莫尔图斯·骨钟
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:960
who: Mortus the Bone Bell, a demon-kin of the white-bone folk and keeper of the oldest bell tower of the Tomb City, who read back the names of a million and seven hundred thousand dead and gave thirteen of his own earliest memories for thirteen who had no name left; a hundred and ninety-four in 779 and looking thirty-two or thirty-three ever since: about 184 cm, tall and thin. Skin pale almost to translucence; a strip of crystal-white bone shows along the left jaw. Short black hair falling a little over the brow. Ice-blue eyes; over the right eye a round monocle of clear reading crystal ringed in fine gold wire. Ink-stained fingers, an old burn scar on the left hand. Nothing hangs at his neck any more. A quiet, exact air with a dry, unsmiling humour.
build: 184 cm, tall and thin: narrow shoulders, long fingers, a very straight back.
palette: bell-tower grey and bone white, ice blue, fine gold wire, a little lamp amber
casual: The robe of a bell-tower keeper: a long grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat, at the corner of the hem an embroidered bell with a notch missing from its rim; a narrow belt with the small cloth pouch of Rain City ash, now nearly empty; a carved bone tag on a cord at his chest, the number of this tower's keeper; the gold-ringed crystal at his right eye. He holds an open name register and a pen in his ink-stained fingers, a calm, exact look.
private: In the bell chamber at night after the twelfth stroke: a plain dark grey wool shirt buttoned to the neck, dark trousers and soft shoes, the crystal still at his eye. He holds in the crook of one arm a small grey cat he has just lifted off the bell rope, a quiet, faintly amused look.
battle: Leading a company of lamp-bearers to a field of the dead: the grey keeper's robe with the notched bell at the hem under a long dark grey hooded travelling cloak, the bone tag at his chest, the reading crystal. He holds up a small lit lamp in one hand and the open register against his chest with the other; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: upright and very still, a level, unblinking gaze through the crystal, holding up a small lit lamp in one hand and the open register against his chest with the other; he does not fight.
formal: On the last night of the year when the old bell is struck twelve times: the keeper's robe of the finest grey wool buttoned to the throat, the notched bell at its hem worked in silver-grey thread, a long pale grey stole hanging from both shoulders, the keeper's bone tag on his chest, the reading crystal at his eye. He stands very straight with the register held to his chest, a grave, polite look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer through the gold-ringed crystal over the right eye, a still, patient look. Cold grey night light from one side and the warm glow of one small lamp set beside a great old bell. Foreground blur: the rim of the huge bone-white bell, a thick bell rope and drifting ash. He wears the grey keeper's robe buttoned to the throat.

name: 卢恩
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1016
who: Rune, a demon-kin boy of the white-bone folk, the youngest of the bell-tower keeper's family of the Tomb City and the apprentice who pulls the bell rope at night; his folk grow very slowly, so he is forty-four but looks seventeen or eighteen: tall, thin and long-limbed, about 179 cm, wholly covered by his clothes. Pale grey skin. The tips of all ten fingers are bare white bone and click faintly when he touches things. His head is shaved very short; on his forehead a small number-mark carved into the bone, and beside it a neat row of twelve short, shallow notches, one for each stroke of the bell. Ice-blue eyes that blink more often than other white-bone folk. A quick, impatient, talkative air; he counts everything.
palette: apprentice grey and bone white, ice blue, faded hemp, a single red thread
casual: His apprentice's clothes: a grey knee-length short robe with the sleeves rolled to the elbow over dark leggings, an old length of bell rope wound twice round his waist, one strand mended with a red thread; a carved bone tag with his number on a cord at his chest; soft-soled shoes that make no sound in the tomb levels. He holds up one hand with the bone fingertips spread, about to count, a quick, eager look.
private: Down from the tower at dawn: a loose long-sleeved grey wool tunic, dark trousers and soft shoes, the old bell rope still at his waist. He runs a bone fingertip along the row of notches on his forehead, a quiet, thoughtful look.
battle: On the tower through the night watch: the grey apprentice robe belted tight with the old bell rope, leather wrist guards, soft shoes, the bone tag at his chest. He holds a heavy coil of thick bell rope in both hands in front of him; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the night-watch outfit: tense and ready, the shoulders squared, the feet planted, a firm expression, holding a heavy coil of thick bell rope in both hands in front of him; he does not fight.
formal: At a rite of the bell-tower keepers: a long grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat and a bell embroidered at the hem, the bone tag on his chest, the old bell rope at his waist, soft shoes. He stands very upright with his hands together in front, a serious look.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the ice-blue eyes looking at the viewer quick and bright, a bone fingertip touching the row of twelve notches on his forehead. Cold grey-blue night light from one side and a warm lamp glow from below. Foreground blur: a frayed bell rope mended with red thread, and dust drifting in a bell tower. He wears the grey apprentice robe.

name: 罗珊·铃尾
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1072
who: Rosanne Belltail, a fox-eared beastfolk woman and long-distance courier of the Belltail family, the great-great-granddaughter of the courier Etan, twenty-nine in 779: about 163 cm, thin and long-legged, able to run all day without losing her breath. Red-brown hair in one thick braid coiled at the nape. Tall red-brown fox ears that turn toward a far-off bell before she does. A full red-brown fox tail with a white tip like frost, three small copper bells tied tight at its root. Amber eyes. Cheeks reddened by the wind and a stripe of peeling sunburn across the tip of the nose. A quick, open, chatty air; she laughs out loud before she smiles.
build: 163 cm, thin and long-legged: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: fox red-brown and frost white, oilcloth olive, copper, a little faded leather
casual: Her courier's clothes: an oilcloth short jacket with the collar turned down and its pockets half sewn shut so no letter can fall out, over a dark wool shirt, slim trousers and boots resoled many times; across her body a letter bag whose mouth is tied three times round with leather cord; at her waist a small water skin and a pouch of salt; the three copper bells at the root of her tail. She stands with one hand on the strap of the letter bag, a bright, laughing look.
private: Resting at the gate of the Tomb City: a loose oatmeal wool tunic with the sleeves pushed up, a dark knitted scarf, slim trousers and soft shoes, the braid let down over one shoulder. She holds a small square of cloth stitched with rows of tiny circles and one small cross, her thumb resting on the cross, a quiet, faraway look.
battle: Running a long road through bad country: the oilcloth jacket buttoned up under a short hooded travelling cloak, leather bracers, cloth wraps round the shins, the letter bag strapped tight across her body, the water skin and salt pouch at her waist, the bells on her tail.
battle_pose: 3) the long-run outfit: ready to sprint, the weight forward, the feet a little apart, a firm expression, one hand gripping the strap of the letter bag across her body; she carries no weapon.
formal: Bringing a letter to a family of the dead in the Tomb City: a clean dark green wool coat buttoned to the collar, a fresh ribbon on her braid, brushed boots, the bells on her tail tied silent with a strip of cloth. She holds a single letter in both hands in front of her, standing very upright, a quiet, serious look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber eyes laughing at the viewer, one fox ear turned aside as if hearing a far-off bell, the white-tipped tail and its three copper bells sweeping across the frame. Cold bright wind-light from one side. Foreground blur: a bundle of letters whose addresses have faded to blank white, drifting dry leaves and the glint of a copper bell. She wears the oilcloth short jacket.

name: 背水的
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1225
who: The Water-Bearer, a demon-kin of the deep-tide snake folk who has no name: in 741 he gave his own name in place of a child's, and since then no one, not even he, can say what he was called; a hundred in 790 and looking about fifty: about 186 cm, tall and wide-backed, steady on his feet. Thin blue-grey scales run in rows down both sides of his neck and shine in the rain; behind his ears a pair of closed gill slits, tighter every year he lives inland. Grey hair cropped very short. Pale jade-green eyes with narrow vertical pupils. Hard calluses on both shoulders from the yoke, one shoulder a little lower than the other. Big hands with thick knuckles, crossed with white scars from cracking ice. A plain face no one remembers seeing. A quiet, patient air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a plain, ordinary man's face of about fifty, weathered and kind, NOT young: pale jade-green eyes with narrow vertical pupils, fine lines at their corners and across the brow; straight grey brows; a closed, patient mouth; thin blue-grey scales along the sides of the neck. Clean skin with very little shading, skin shadows a soft cool tone.
build: 186 cm, tall, wide-shouldered and thick-backed, one shoulder a little lower than the other from the yoke.
palette: blue-grey scales and grey, undyed patched homespun, straw yellow, wet wood brown, a little copper
casual: His water-carrier's clothes: a shirt and trousers of coarse undyed homespun patched layer upon layer, a length of straw rope tied round the waist, worn leather boots; across his shoulders a wooden yoke with a wooden water bucket hanging from each end. Nothing hangs at his neck: he has no name to carve on a stone tag. He stands steady under the yoke, a patient, quiet look.
private: In the little shed at the mouth of the stone forest: the same patched homespun with an old knitted shawl over the shoulders against the damp, the yoke set aside. He holds the dented copper water pot of the stone forest gate in one hand and a tin cup in the other, about to pour for someone, a mild look.
battle: Walking at the head of the stone-bearers into the fog: the patched homespun belted with the straw rope, cloth wraps round the shins, worn boots, a rough grey stone slab roped onto his back. He grips the ropes at his chest with both hands; he carries no weapon.
battle_pose: 3) the stone-bearing outfit: braced under a heavy load, the knees a little bent and the feet planted, a calm, steady expression, a rough grey stone slab, no wider than his back, roped onto his back, both hands gripping the ropes at his chest; he carries no weapon.
formal: On the winter morning when he carries water to Naura's door: the patched homespun washed clean, a plain dark grey wool coat over it buttoned up, the straw rope retied, the boots brushed. He stands very upright holding the copper water pot in both hands in front of him, a quiet, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale jade-green eyes looking at the viewer kindly, as if he knows you though you do not know him, raindrops beading on the blue-grey scales of his neck. Cold grey fog light from one side. Foreground blur: drifting fog, the rim of a wooden bucket spilling water and the rough edge of a standing stone. He wears the patched homespun with the wooden yoke across his shoulders.

name: 叶琳·雨凿
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1281
who: Yelin Rainchisel, a tiefling stonecutter, third generation of the caravan's westward stonecutters, twenty-five in 790: of middle height, about 163 cm, sturdy, her arms all sinew from the hammer. Misty blue hair cut level with the ears and tied back with a strip of cloth. A pair of small horns at the temples curving back, stone grey, the tips ground round on a whetstone when she was a child. Fair skin, faint pale grey tiefling lines like stone grain on the forearms. Copper eyes that linger on letters longer than on people. Stone dust always on her eyelashes. A thick callus in the web of the right hand, the left thumbnail blackened by a hammer. A thin chisel tucked behind one ear. At her neck a small stone tag she carved herself at fifteen, crooked. A quick-handed, stubborn, careful air.
build: 163 cm, sturdy and strong-armed, the arms all sinew: a small bust, a firm waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: misty blue and stone grey, dusty canvas grey, worn leather brown, a little iron
casual: Her stonecutter's work clothes: a dusty grey canvas work suit with leather patches sewn on the knees and elbows, the collar open; a leather belt hung with seven chisels of different sizes and a hammer; on her back a wooden box holding stone powder, an ink line and a whetstone; the crooked stone tag at her neck and a thin chisel behind one ear. She holds a hammer and a chisel, a quick, sharp look.
private: In the stonecutters' yard after work: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, a grey wool vest, canvas trousers, the misty blue hair untied and dusty. She holds a blank stone in one hand and a whetstone in the other, grinding the stone smooth, a quiet, stubborn look.
battle: Working at the edge of the fog: the canvas work suit belted tight, leather gauntlets, a hooded grey canvas cloak against the damp, the box of tools on her back, the crooked stone tag at her neck. She holds the hammer and a chisel ready to strike.
battle_pose: 3) the field outfit: tense and ready, the shoulders squared, the feet planted, a firm expression, a hammer held ready at shoulder height in one hand and a chisel in the other, as if about to strike stone; she does not fight.
formal: At the unveiling of a name-stone in a western camp city: the canvas work suit brushed clean and the leather patches oiled, a clean dark grey wool coat over it, the hair freshly tied back with a new strip of cloth, the crooked stone tag worn outside the coat. She stands very upright with the hammer held at her side, a serious look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the copper eyes intent on something just past the viewer, flecks of stone dust on her eyelashes, the hammer raised beside her face. Cool rain light from one side. Foreground blur: raindrops, flying stone chips and the crooked stone tag on its cord. She wears the dusty grey canvas work suit.

name: 图尔本
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1432
who: Turben, a demon-kin of the white-bone folk who has spent sixty years digging a chain of wells under the Famine Plain, a name carved at the bottom of every shaft; eighty-one in 851 and looking twenty-seven or twenty-eight: about 181 cm, tall and thin with narrow shoulders and long arms. White skin; the knuckles and wrist bones shine white. Earth under his fingernails that sixty years have not washed out. Short, untidy pale sand-coloured hair with dust in it. Ice-blue eyes that stay open all night. Part of the rim of his left ear worn flat from pressing it to well walls to listen for water. An old injury in the right shoulder from a collapsed well. A slow, steady air; he speaks in numbers.
build: 181 cm, tall and thin: narrow shoulders, long arms, big bony knuckles.
palette: earth brown and well dust, bone white, ice blue, copper lamp, wet hemp
casual: His well-digger's clothes: a shirt and trousers of brown coarse cloth, the knees and elbows patched with two layers of leather, the collar open; round his waist a coiled measuring cord with a knot at every foot; at his belt a short pick, a carving knife and a copper oil lamp; boots that are always wet. He holds a length of the knotted cord in his hands, counting the knots, a calm, steady look.
private: By the new pool at the heart of the plain: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves pushed up, brown trousers rolled to the shin, the wet boots on. He holds out a tin cup of water brought from outside the plain, offering it, a mild, dry smile.
battle: Going down a frozen shaft in winter: the patched brown clothes under a thick oilcloth coat, leather gloves, a cloth for the nose and mouth hanging loose at the neck, the copper oil lamp lit at his belt. He grips the short pick in one hand, the knotted cord coiled over the other shoulder.
battle_pose: 3) the well outfit: braced and ready, the feet planted, a firm expression, the short pick gripped in one hand and the knotted measuring cord coiled over the other shoulder; he is a digger, not a fighter.
formal: At the unveiling of the stone at the heart of the plain, where he read out four thousand one hundred and twelve names: the brown clothes washed clean, a plain dark wool coat over them buttoned up, the knotted cord coiled neatly at his waist. He stands very upright with his hands folded over the coiled cord, a grave look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the ice-blue eyes looking up at the viewer as if from the bottom of a well, a faint, dry smile. A shaft of pale daylight falls from above on one side into the dark, warm copper lamplight below. Foreground blur: dripping water, a knotted cord and crumbs of earth. He wears the brown coarse cloth clothes with leather on the elbows.

name: 哈莎·碗主
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1488
who: Hasha Bowlkeeper, a demon-kin woman of the feast-born bloodline and daughter of the bowl-keeping family who served the high seat of the Famine Plain, twenty in 851 and looking eighteen or nineteen: about 163 cm, thin and fine-boned, used to hunger. High cheekbones. Dark red hair in one thick braid. Dark red eyes that glow at night. Lips chapped from hunger. On the palm of her left hand a ring of dark red like the rim of a bowl, there since birth; she keeps that hand closed. A careful, quiet, exact air: she weighs everything and writes it down, and the first thing she asks anyone is whether they have eaten.
build: 163 cm, thin and fine-boned: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: faded ochre red, dark red, charcoal black, old copper, pale wood
casual: Her bowl-keeper's robe: a long ochre-red robe washed pale, a ring of bowl-rim pattern embroidered at each cuff, a narrow belt hung with a wooden tally board, a stick of charcoal and her father's copper steelyard; plain shoes. She holds the tally board and the charcoal, her left hand closed, a careful, questioning look.
private: After the high seat fell: a plain long dark wool dress with long sleeves, a grey shawl, soft shoes, the braid over one shoulder. She holds an empty stone bowl in both hands and looks into it, a quiet, thoughtful look.
battle: On the last night of the year at the edge of the crater: the ochre-red robe belted tight under a dark hooded cloak against the cold, the copper steelyard at her waist. She holds an empty stone bowl turned upside down in both hands, about to set it on the ground.
battle_pose: 3) the last-night outfit: tense and still, the shoulders squared, the feet planted, a firm expression, holding an empty stone bowl turned upside down in both hands; she does not fight.
formal: As the daughter of the seat-priest at a rite of the bowl: the bowl-keepers' full robe, a long deep ochre-red robe with wide bands of bowl-rim pattern at the cuffs and hem, a dark red sash with the copper steelyard hung from it. She stands very upright with her hands folded, the left still closed, a solemn, guarded look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the dark red eyes glowing faintly in the dusk as she looks at the viewer as if asking whether they have eaten, a stone bowl held near her chin. Cold blue dusk light from one side over a bare plain. Foreground blur: the rim of an empty stone bowl, drifting chaff of black-eared grain and the corner of a wooden tally board. She wears the faded ochre-red robe.

name: 黛洛
src: 山铜纪/山铜纪时段_五_七城的年月.md:1672
who: Delo, a demon-kin woman of the nightmare bloodline, youngest daughter of the Mirror Hall family of the mirror city, who keeps the night watch over the children of the western camp and walks into their bad dreams to lead them out; a hundred and nine in 742 and looking about thirty: small and slight, about 156 cm, light-stepped. Deep violet hair hanging below the waist, its ends glinting faintly in the dark as if dusted with fine ash. Short pointed ears. Violet eyes that look first at the shadows under your eyes. A small face that always looks not quite awake. A folded scrap of paper tucked into one cuff. A gentle, soft-spoken, careful air; she has not gone home in a hundred years.
build: 156 cm, small and slight: a small bust, a very narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: deep violet and dusk grey, pale lavender, worn copper, tin grey, a little lamp amber
casual: Her night-watch clothes: a long deep grey coat, its hem mended many times, a folded scrap of paper tucked into one cuff, over a plain dark dress; a small cloth bag at her waist holding a chipped copper coin and a tin cup; soft boots. She holds the little tin cup in both hands, a soft, attentive look.
private: In her tent in the children's quarter at night: a loose dark knitted cardigan over a long dark dress, thick socks, the long hair in a loose plait over one shoulder. She holds the day's note, a scrap of paper written by a child, reading it with a small smile.
battle: Going down into a child's nightmare: the long deep grey coat buttoned to the collar, the cloth bag at her waist, soft boots. One hand is raised with a faint glitter of sleep-sand at the fingertips; the other holds the tin cup.
battle_pose: 3) the dream-walking outfit: tense and focused, the shoulders squared, a firm, quiet expression, one hand raised with a faint glitter of sand-like light at the fingertips, the other holding the tin cup; she carries no weapon.
formal: At the caravan's memorial for its dead: a long dark violet-grey robe with a high collar buttoned to the throat and close cuffs, a pale grey shawl over the shoulders, the cloth bag at her waist. She stands very upright with her hands folded, a quiet, gentle look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the violet eyes looking at the viewer softly, as if checking whether you have slept, a small tired smile. Warm lamplight from inside a tent on one side against the deep blue night. Foreground blur: the fold of a tent flap, a tin cup and her own shadow lagging a little behind on the canvas. She wears the long deep grey coat.
